responsibilities: Collaborate with Ecommerce BI Analysts to understand business needs and translate them into efficient data structures.
Enable analysts to focus on delivering insights by ensuring timely access to curated, high-quality datasets.
Partner with Data Engineers to ensure data availability in staging environments.
Own the transformation layer between staging and analytics-ready datasets, applying business logic to create trusted sources for analysis.
Develop and manage layered transformation workflows that promote modularity, traceability, and alignment with governance and AI-readiness standards.
Build and maintain structured, reusable datasets using dbt or similar transformation tools, applying scalable logic to support analytics across ecommerce products.
Maintain documentation, testing protocols, and data quality standards.

Ensure data and models from on-prem applications, Google Analytics and other sources support key ecommerce metrics related to site search, customer behavior, product performance, and other relevant measures.
Lead development of scalable, modular data models (staging, intermediate, mart) that support traceability and reduce duplicative effort.
Optimize transformation logic for performance and maintainability.
Define and enforce documentation and lineage standards for analytics datasets.
Work closely with cross-functional product teams to ensure data models align with customer experience goals and ecommerce KPIs.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Maintain documentation, testing protocols, and data quality standards.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: the bullets stack up quality language -- "Maintain documentation, testing protocols, and data quality standards." -- with no speed or shipping vocabulary anywhere.
evidence.domain_risk: Work closely with cross-functional product teams to ensure data models align with customer experience goals and ecommerce KPIs.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: errors hit ecommerce reporting and "ecommerce KPIs", with no financial-reporting, audit or regulatory language.
evidence.collaboration_width: Ecommerce BI Analysts; Data Engineers; cross-functional product teams
evidence.data_team_maturity: Partner with Data Engineers to ensure data availability in staging environments.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid: separate BI analyst and data engineer groups already exist and staging environments are in place -- "Partner with Data Engineers to ensure data availability in staging environments."
evidence.jd_authorship: Lead development of scalable, modular data models (staging, intermediate, mart) that support traceability and reduce duplicative effort.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Hiring manager: the bullets name the actual layering -- "(staging, intermediate, mart)" -- and the tools used to build it, so the daily work is legible.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Enable analysts to focus on delivering insights by ensuring timely access to curated, high-quality datasets.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Internal data: the primary audience is the BI analyst group -- "Enable analysts to focus on delivering insights" -- with product teams a secondary consumer.
evidence.autonomy_level: Own the transformation layer between staging and analytics-ready datasets
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: the role owns and sets the standard, not just delivers -- "Own the transformation layer" and "Define and enforce documentation and lineage standards".
evidence.ai_role: alignment with governance and AI-readiness standards
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI enabler: the candidate builds the transformation layer to an "AI-readiness" standard, so AI consumes their output rather than assisting their coding.
evidence.testing_framing: Maintain documentation, testing protocols, and data quality standards.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: testing sits in the responsibility bullets under an ownership verb -- "Maintain documentation, testing protocols, and data quality standards." -- not in a tool list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: applying business logic to create trusted sources for analysis
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: trust in the data is a stated concern -- "create trusted sources for analysis" -- but the dominant framing is enabling analysts, with no compliance or incident register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build and maintain structured, reusable datasets using dbt or similar transformation tools
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed: new model building sits alongside upkeep -- "Build and maintain structured, reusable datasets" and "Optimize transformation logic for performance and maintainability".
evidence.loss_aversion: "Own the transformation layer between staging and analytics-ready datasets, applying business logic to create trusted sources for analysis." -- the risk being managed is analysts building on untrusted data, not regulatory exposure.
